summary: Full diagnostic sweep of all 35 admin routes as logged-in Preview admin (test@aurem.dev). Every route renders (no persistent crash / no whitelist). Vast majority show REAL live data from Mongo/Stripe/OpenRouter. Main systemic issue: an aggressive global rate-limiter (Redis unavailable, in-memory fallback) causes CASCADE 429 errors when the admin shell fires many widget requests in parallel, which trips the react error boundary and shows 'Something went wrong loading this page' on ~6 routes intermittently. A single reload usually recovers the page. Also identified a handful of data-source mismatches (Token P&L $0 vs Agent Perf real cost; Cockpit MRR 'No data yet' vs $57 revenue widget on same page; Parliament runs=0 in system-stats vs 750+ council calls visible elsewhere; Architecture Persona Quality Score '—'). No auth/console-error hard crashes on any route.

critical.issue: Redis unavailable → in-memory per-process rate limiter is too strict and triggers 429 storms when admin panel loads multiple widgets in parallel. When 429 fires the middleware ALSO raises RuntimeError('No response returned.') (see backend.err.log). This cascades: React ErrorBoundary tries to POST /api/admin/errors/report which is ALSO rate-limited → infinite retry loop → 'Something went wrong loading this page' on ~6 admin routes. Reload usually clears it because it's a per-process burst. Fix: raise the admin-endpoint rate-limit ceiling (or exempt authenticated admin JWT), start Redis on 127.0.0.1:6379 in preview, and CRITICALLY exempt /api/admin/errors/report from the limiter so the error boundary can always report.

minor.issue: ~4210 ms server-side response — user sees 'Loading QA status…' with no spinner for 4+ seconds. Consider caching /api/admin/qa/status output.

'MRR (LIVE) — No data yet' shown while same page cockpit badge shows REVENUE 30d $57. MRR live projection not wired to same Stripe/catalog_projection source.

Persistent 'Frontend bundle ≠ production backend — bundle may be stale' warning — either genuine drift or the check itself is comparing wrong SHAs.

critical_code_review_comments: backend/main.py:2374 — the rate_limit_guard raises RuntimeError('No response returned.') on the 429 branch instead of returning a proper 429 JSONResponse. This surfaces as a 500 in downstream and confuses the front-end error boundary. Return a Response object explicitly.
Error-report endpoint (/api/admin/errors/report) MUST be exempt from rate-limiting — otherwise the ErrorBoundary can't log its own error and retries in a loop.

Multiple admin pages fetch the same core stats independently (cockpit revenue, dashboard users, personal-track MRR, token-pnl revenue) — duplicated queries + inconsistent aggregates. Extract a single admin/analytics/summary endpoint.
Preview env has no Redis running; the rate_limiter falls back to per-process in-memory (see services/rate_limiter.py). This is not viable for even light admin usage.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Full 35-route admin panel audit complete. All routes render. The main systemic bug is the global rate limiter + missing Redis + non-exempt errors/report endpoint (backend/main.py:2374). Secondary bugs are data-source inconsistencies between: (1) /admin/token-pnl showing $0 vs agent-perf showing real cost, (2) /admin/cockpit MRR 'No data yet' vs $57 revenue on same page, (3) /admin/system-stats Parliament runs=0 vs 750+ council calls, (4) /admin/architecture Persona Quality '—' with 86 runs. rca_of_the_issue: Systemic 429 cascade RCA: (1) Preview has no Redis on 127.0.0.1:6379, so backend/services/rate_limiter.py falls back to in-memory per-process. (2) Admin panel widgets fire 5–15 API calls in parallel on tab-switch, breaching the per-process burst. (3) When limiter returns 429, backend/main.py:2374 _global_rate_limit_guard raises RuntimeError('No response returned.') instead of returning a 429 Response, so downstream marks the request failed. (4) React ErrorBoundary catches 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' from the lazy admin route and tries to POST /api/admin/errors/report, which is ITSELF rate-limited → infinite retry loop → user stuck on 'Something went wrong loading this page'. (5) Reload usually recovers because the per-process burst window resets. Fix by (a) exempting authenticated admin JWT from the burst limit, (b) returning a proper 429 Response object from _global_rate_limit_guard, (c) hard-exempting /api/admin/errors/report.
